post.caption: Gold-filled jewelry needs only five percent gold. In the United States, that means at least one twentieth of the total weight, in a layer of ten karat gold or better that covers every surface and is bonded to a base metal core by mechanical means. The layer is much thicker than regular plating, so it lasts longer. Gold electroplate needs only 0.175 microns of gold. Vermeil has a sterling silver base under its gold, and its gold layer must be at least ten karat and 2.5 microns thick. Rolled gold plate has half as much gold as gold-filled, which is one fortieth of the total weight.
